citation: Tolan, P., Elreda, L. M., Bradshaw, C. P., Downer, J. T., & Ialongo, N. (2020). Randomized trial testing the integration of the Good Behavior Game and MyTeachingPartner™: The moderating role of distress among new teachers on student outcomes. Journal of School Psychology, 78, 75-95. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsp.2019.12.002
design: RCT; teacher/class-level random assignment (blocked on school and district) of 188 early-career K-3 teachers (grades K-3, first three years of teaching) from 72 schools across three large urban US school districts (Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Prince George's County); GBG+MyTeachingPartner combined classroom-management/teacher-PD intervention (2-day workshop + ~8 biweekly MTP coaching cycles) vs business-as-usual control. Achievement (WJ III) collected only for Cohorts 1 & 2 = 95 teachers; behavioral outcomes for full 188. Student achievement data aggregated to classroom (teacher) level; analyzed via single-level multiple linear regression in MPlus 8 with FIML, controlling for pretest and teacher/student/school covariates.
problems: (1) The ONLY full-sample TPD-vs-control achievement contrast available is the non-significant main-effect 'Treatment group' coefficient in Table 5 (Reading B=0.03 SE 0.03; Math B=-0.01 SE 0.04), in the WJ-III grade-adjusted composite metric. The paper's headline achievement findings (reading d=0.18, math d=0.11) are SUBGROUP/MODERATED effects for the highest-risk subset only (high baseline teacher distress + high baseline classroom disruptive behavior); these are NOT full-sample and are recorded as notes/separate subgroup rows below (is_full_sample=false). (2) g for the two full-sample main effects was computed as d=B/SD_post using the full-sample post-test composite SD from Table 2 (Reading 0.88, Math 1.04), the same pooled-SD basis the authors used for their reported d's; g_se=SE/SD. (3) Exact intervention/control split of the 95 achievement teachers is not reported; full-ITT split was 94/94 (CONSORT Fig. 1), so n_t/n_c for the achievement subsample are left null and J/df use the 95-teacher analytic N (units = classrooms). (4) Clustering: analysis is at the teacher/classroom level (students were aggregated up to classroom mean before analysis), so the unit of analysis IS the cluster; the model is single-level on classroom means (design effect for teacher-within-school clustering reported as 1.01-1.34, treated as negligible by authors); cluster_adjusted=true at the classroom level. n_clusters = 95 teachers/classrooms (achievement subsample). (5) Skipped non-academic outcomes per spec: student socially disruptive behavior, student off-task behavior, student compliance (classroom-observation behavioral/SEL measures, ASSIST); all teacher-practice/distress/fidelity measures. Behavioral main effects were also null (Table 4); behavioral subgroup d's were 0.45-0.70.

effect_sizes.arm_label: GBG+MTP vs business-as-usual control (full sample, main effect)
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock-Johnson III Tests of Achievement, Reading composite (Reading Fluency + Reading Comprehension), grade-adjusted
effect_sizes.g_method: d = B/SD_post = 0.03/0.88 using full-sample post-test composite SD (Table 2); g = J*d, J=0.9919 (df=N-2, N=95 classrooms); g_se = J*(SE/SD) = 0.9919*(0.03/0.88). Impact_estimate is the pretest-adjusted 'Treatment group' regression coefficient from Table 5. mean_t/mean_c/sd reported are raw full-sample post-test composite values (Table 2), shown for reference only; g is from the adjusted coefficient.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. 87 Table 5 (Treatment group coefficient, Reading composite); p. 80 Table 2 (post-test means/SDs)
effect_sizes.notes: Full-sample TPD-vs-control main effect on reading achievement; NON-significant (no main effects of intervention in any model). Outcome aggregated to classroom level; unit of analysis = teacher/classroom (95 classrooms, Cohorts 1 & 2 only). WJ III is a standardized/independent norm-referenced test. Authors report a moderated reading d=0.18 ONLY for the highest-risk subgroup (high distress + high disruption) -- see separate subgroup row, not full-sample.
